q: A camera is an optical instrument that forms and records an image of an object. The image may be recorded on film or detected by an _____ sensor.
e: A camera forms and records an image of an object on film or on an electronic sensor. A convex lens throws a real inverted image onto that screen. Magnetic or thermal sensors are not the usual picture-taker. Camera is an optical instrument that forms cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: In a camera, a _____ lens focuses the light from the object to form a real inverted image.
e: A convex lens converges light and can form a real inverted image. Cameras, microscope objectives and the eyelens for near vision all use extra converging power. A camera and a microscope objective need a convex converging lens.

q: A _____ is placed behind the convex lens to control the amount of light energy falling on the film.
e: The diaphragm sits behind the convex lens and controls how much light energy hits the film. It changes aperture diameter, quoted as an f-number. The shutter times the light; the diaphragm sets the amount.

q: The aperture is a circular opening through which the light passes, and its size is expressed in terms of _____.
e: Aperture is the circular opening light passes through. f-number is focal length over diameter; smaller f-number means a wider hole. Aperture size is an f-number, not an ISO rating.

q: The f-number of a camera is the ratio of the _____ of the lens to the diameter of aperture.
e: f-number is focal length of the lens divided by aperture diameter. Small f-number, wide aperture, more light. f-number is f/D, focal length over diameter.

q: When taking a photograph in bright light a _____ f-number must be used.
e: f-number is focal length of the lens divided by aperture diameter. Small f-number, wide aperture, more light. Bright light wants a large f-number, a stopped-down hole.

q: A _____ controls the time during which light enters the camera through the lens.
e: The shutter times how long light may enter through the lens. Shutter speed is quoted as that exposure time. The focusing ring sharpens; it does not time the exposure.

q: The shutter speed is expressed in terms of the _____ time.
e: The shutter times how long light may enter through the lens. Shutter speed is quoted as that exposure time. The receptor-free patch is the blind spot.

q: In a digital camera, the film is replaced by an electronic sensor which is made up of millions of tiny _____.
e: A digital sensor is millions of tiny pixels that respond to light. They store the image digitally, not analogously. The sensor is described as pixels, not diodes.

q: The film consists of a thin layer of chemical compounds of _____.
e: Photographic film is a thin layer of silver compounds. Those grains blacken where light hits. The film chemistry in this chapter is silver, not silicon.
